name: Lystra
overview: Lystra, one of the cities of Lycaonia, served as a refuge for Paul and Barnabas as they fled persecution from Iconium, where they continued to boldly preach the gospel. In this city, Paul healed a man crippled from birth, an act that led the local people to mistakenly worship them as gods. This event highlights both the power of faith and the challenges of proclaiming Christ in a pagan context. Furthermore, Lystra became a foundational center for the early church, where Paul and Barnabas ordained elders to shepherd the congregation, and where Timothy, a key companion of Paul, resided.
